papers.title: Cortical layer 6b mediates state-dependent changes in brain activity and effects of orexin on waking and sleep.
papers.summary: The study silenced a subset of cortical layer 6b neurons in mice and found reduced EEG power, particularly in NREM sleep, and a slowing of theta frequency during wake and REM sleep. The response to orexin A was altered, suggesting L6b neurons regulate state-dependent brain oscillations.

papers.title: Adaptive reorganization of local sleep and prelimbic cortical circuits predict behavioral resilience to social defeat stress.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: The study recorded prelimbic cortex activity in mice before and after social defeat stress, finding that resilient mice had stronger coupling between neuronal OFF-periods and slow-waves at baseline and showed reorganization of OFF-period patterns after stress. This suggests a capacity for flexible network redistribution during NREM sleep predicts resilience.

papers.title: "Local modulation of sleep slow waves depends on timing between auditory stimuli" [NeuroImage, 322 (2025) 121561].
papers.summary: This is a published erratum for the article 'Local modulation of sleep slow waves depends on timing between auditory stimuli'. It contains no new scientific content.

papers.title: REM sleep prefrontal high-frequency oscillation chains mediate distinct cortical - hippocampal reactivation patterns compared to NREM sleep.
papers.summary: This study in rodents identifies prefrontal cortical high-frequency oscillation (HFO) chains during REM sleep that phase-modulate with theta oscillations and coordinate sparse hippocampal-cortical reactivation of spatial memories, contrasting with NREM ripples. A cortical network model incorporating acetylcholine effects reproduces these distinct REM and NREM activity patterns, linking REM HFOs to memory consolidation.

papers.title: Circadian reprogramming of inflammation and metabolism in chronic kidney disease.
papers.summary: This study performed time-series RNA-seq on kidneys from CKD mice, showing disrupted circadian transcriptome with acquired rhythmicity in immune-inflammatory genes and decreased rhythmicity in metabolic genes. Dapagliflozin partially restored core clock gene rhythms and improved renal function.

papers.title: Are infraslow oscillations the missing link between sleep and Alzheimer's?
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: The study analyzed NREM sleep EEG in Alzheimer's disease (AD) participants and controls, finding reduced infraslow oscillation (ISO) peak amplitude in AD with preserved frequency and bandwidth. ISO amplitude trended with Aβ42/40, and bandwidth was associated with NfL, suggesting ISO may link sleep and AD pathology.

papers.title: Tracing melanin-concentrating hormone function: decades of memory research and emerging links to Alzheimer's disease.
papers.summary: This mini-review summarizes studies on melanin-concentrating hormone (MCH) in memory, noting its complex role in promoting consolidation, inducing forgetting during REM sleep, or negatively regulating memory formation. It also discusses emerging links to Alzheimer's disease, including therapeutic potential and effects on sleep architecture.

papers.title: Evaluate the effectiveness of cognitive stimulation and physiological dynamization on sleep inertia.
papers.summary: This randomized controlled trial evaluated cognitive stimulation and physiological dynamization as countermeasures for sleep inertia after normal and recovery sleep. Physiological dynamization significantly reduced reaction time and lapses within 20 minutes post-awakening, suggesting it is a promising intervention.

papers.title: Sleep and Overnight Cardiovascular Outcomes During the First Week on a Temperature-Controlled Sleep Surface: Stratified by Baseline Performance
papers.summary: In an open-label study of 171 adults, a temperature-controlled sleep surface increased total sleep time and improved overnight cardiovascular measures, with the largest gains observed in those with the poorest baseline sleep. Stratification by baseline performance revealed significant improvements in sleep efficiency, REM, deep sleep, and HRV in the most deficient quartiles.

papers.title: Diurnal variation in subjective states and cognitive performance: Empirical evidence from laboratory and real-world work settings.
papers.summary: The study assessed subjective states and cognitive performance at multiple times of day in both laboratory and real work settings. Results showed a post-lunch decline in sleepiness and vitality, and cognitive performance varied by task, with sustained attention best in the morning and working memory better in the afternoon.

papers.title: Muscle-Specific Upregulation of Timeless Mediates Exercise-Induced Amelioration of Age-Related Circadian Rhythm Disruption and Cardiac Dysfunction in Drosophila.
papers.summary: Using Drosophila, this study showed that muscle-specific knockdown of Timeless accelerates age-related circadian and cardiac dysfunction, while overexpression delays it. A 4-week endurance exercise regimen counteracted the effects of knockdown and further improved outcomes in aged flies, suggesting exercise acts through Timeless upregulation.

papers.title: Utility of Cephalometry and Acoustic Pharyngometry for the Assessment of Moderate to Severe Obstructive Sleep Apnea Before Treatment in Childhood.
papers.summary: Cross-sectional study of 205 children with moderate-to-severe OSA found that cephalometric indices (FMA and hyoid bone distance) were independently associated with OAHI, but with weak explanatory power. Acoustic pharyngometry measures correlated with height and FMIA, indicating cephalometry provides additional endotypic information.

papers.title: Neurophysiological Signatures of Negative Symptom Improvement After High-Definition Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation: A Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation-Electroencephalography Study.
papers.summary: This study combined TMS-EEG and a randomized double-blind trial to show that HD-tDCS targeting the left DLPFC improves negative symptoms in schizophrenia, with N100 normalization as a potential biomarker. The improvement in negative symptoms was specifically associated with N100 changes, suggesting restoration of cortical inhibition.

papers.title: Higher signal diversity, network dysregulation, and increased well-being under DMT administration: An EEG study.
papers.summary: EEG recordings in 13 healthy participants under intravenous DMT revealed reduced functional connectivity, increased signal complexity in beta/gamma bands, and decreased complexity in delta/theta/alpha bands. DMT also increased arousal and well-being correlates, supporting the entropic brain theory.

papers.title: Convergent Functional Connectivity Alterations in ADHD Revealed by EEG: A Systematic Review Across Methods, States and Spatial Scales.
papers.summary: This systematic review synthesized 37 EEG functional connectivity studies in ADHD, finding convergent patterns of reduced posterior integration with frontal compensation and altered network organization. These EEG findings parallel fMRI evidence, supporting EEG as a translational tool for ADHD.

papers.title: Circadian Rhythm Disruption in Alzheimer's Disease: Molecular Mechanisms, Clinical Implications, and Therapeutic Approaches.
papers.summary: This review examines the interplay between circadian rhythm disruption and Alzheimer's disease, highlighting that circadian gene dysregulation exacerbates tau and amyloid pathology, and discusses therapeutic approaches like light therapy and melatonin. It emphasizes the need for integrated and personalized circadian-based therapies.

papers.title: [Research progress on polysomnographic characteristics and cognitive function in perimenopausal obstructive sleep apnea].
papers.journal: Zhonghua jie he he hu xi za zhi = Zhonghua jiehe he huxi zazhi = Chinese journal of tuberculosis and respiratory diseases
papers.summary: This review summarizes the polysomnographic characteristics of perimenopausal women with OSA, identifying a unique pattern of REM-predominant hypopneas and intermittent hypoxia linked to cognitive decline. It advocates for multidimensional assessment beyond AHI for early identification and management.

papers.title: Early-life GABA-A receptor blockade with bicuculline attenuates anxiety-like behaviors and cognitive deficits induced by 24-hr sleep deprivation in adult male rats.
papers.journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
papers.summary: This study in male rats found that early-life transient blockade of GABA-A receptors with bicuculline prevented cognitive deficits and anxiety-like behaviors induced by 24-hr sleep deprivation in adulthood, and restored hippocampal antioxidant enzyme activities and MDA levels. This suggests a developmental role of early GABAergic signaling in resilience to sleep loss.

papers.title: Preoperative Resting-State EEG Features Associated With Chronic Postoperative Pain After Breast Cancer Surgery: A Prospective Cohort Study.
papers.summary: In a prospective cohort of breast cancer surgery patients, higher preoperative resting-state frontal gamma power and connectivity were associated with clinically significant chronic postoperative pain at 3 months. The study suggests frontal gamma activity may reflect baseline neurophysiological vulnerability to chronic pain.

papers.title: Whole-brain mapping of choline acetyltransferase neurons expression in tree shrew compared with mice.
papers.summary: This study systematically mapped the whole-brain distribution and morphology of choline acetyltransferase-immunoreactive (ChAT-ir) neurons in the tree shrew and compared them with those in mice, revealing key interspecies differences such as absence of cortical ChAT-ir neurons in the tree shrew and higher density in specific subcortical nuclei. The findings provide a structural framework for studying cholinergic roles in neural functions.

papers.title: Reliability of short-term measurements of heart rate variability (HRV) in patients with non-permanent atrial fibrillation.
papers.summary: This study evaluated the reliability of short-term heart rate variability (HRV) measurements from 48-h Holter recordings in patients with non-permanent atrial fibrillation, finding poor absolute reliability (limits of agreement up to several hundred percent) and suggesting limited use for individual-level clinical interpretation.

papers.title: An Intraoperative EEG Biomarker for Postoperative Delirium Predicting Based on Interpretable Deep Learning Framework.
papers.summary: This study developed an interpretable deep learning framework using intraoperative EEG to predict postoperative delirium with high accuracy, identifying a frontal 2-12 Hz oscillation biomarker. The biomarker was validated externally, supporting its use for early warning and individualized care.

papers.title: The Circadian Skin: Chronobiology as a New Frontier in Dermatological Therapy.
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes evidence that skin has intrinsic circadian clocks regulating physiology and disease processes, and highlights chronodermatology as a promising approach. However, it notes most therapeutic applications require more prospective human trials before clinical recommendation.

papers.title: Wearable Sensors Offer Opportunities for Phenotyping Perinatal Mood Disorders: a Narrative Review.
papers.summary: This narrative review discusses how wearable sensors can monitor sleep, circadian rhythms, and hormonal changes to phenotype perinatal mood disorders, potentially enabling earlier diagnosis and personalized interventions. It highlights the need for continuous monitoring to differentiate risk and improve maternal well-being.

papers.title: Save your friend, strike your enemy! How sex and handedness influence EEG signatures of cooperative and competitive behaviour.
papers.summary: In a Go/NoGo task with EEG, this study investigated how sex and handedness affect neural signatures of cooperative and competitive behavior, finding that accuracy was higher in males, and response times were faster in the enemy condition, with some EEG differences consistent with the evolutionarily stable strategy hypothesis.

papers.title: Mapping the Evidence for Operator Syndrome Among Special Operations Forces: A Scoping Review.
papers.summary: This scoping review systematically mapped the evidence for 'Operator Syndrome' in Special Operations Forces, identifying six sources. It found the construct is conceptually heterogeneous with no consensus definition, limited empirical support, and substantial overlap with other conditions such as mild traumatic brain injury and PTSD.

papers.title: Long-term ambient benzene exposure, acceleration of biological aging, and risk of incident psychiatric disorders: A cohort study in the UK Biobank.
papers.summary: In a UK Biobank cohort of 410,207 participants, long-term ambient benzene exposure was associated with increased risks of psychiatric disorders, including multiple psychiatric disorders, with accelerated biological aging partially mediating the associations.

papers.title: Association between circadian syndrome and frailty progression among middle-aged and older adults in China: A longitudinal study based on CHARLS.
papers.summary: This longitudinal study of 7330 Chinese adults found that circadian syndrome (CircS) at baseline was associated with higher risks of moderate-rising and high-stable frailty trajectories, and that a greater number of CircS components was linked to faster increases in frailty index over time.

papers.title: Functional brain connectivity from the fetal period through infancy: A narrative review of resting-state fMRI studies.
papers.summary: This narrative review synthesizes human resting-state fMRI studies from the fetal period through infancy, highlighting hierarchical functional network development with early stabilization of sensorimotor systems and prolonged refinement of higher-order association systems, and associations with prematurity, early environments, and later neurodevelopmental outcomes.

papers.title: Routine Blood Indicators Combined With Sleep Questionnaires for the Identification of Cognitive Impairment in Parkinson's Disease: A Cross-Sectional Study With a Leakage-Free Nested Modeling Framework.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study of 347 Parkinson's disease patients developed a leakage-free nested modeling framework combining routine blood indicators and sleep questionnaires to identify cognitive impairment, achieving a test-set AUC of 0.943 in the full logistic regression model, which significantly outperformed a clinical baseline model.

papers.title: [Collaborative diagnosis and treatment of children with extremely severe obstructive sleep apnea involving multi-system damage].
papers.journal: Zhonghua er bi yan hou tou jing wai ke za zhi = Chinese journal of otorhinolaryngology head and neck surgery
papers.summary: This case series describes the multidisciplinary management of three children with extremely severe obstructive sleep apnea and multisystem damage, all of whom underwent tonsillectomy and adenoidectomy after stabilization and had complete symptomatic relief at one-year follow-up.

papers.title: Maladaptive coping strategies mediate the relationship between perceived differential treatment and sleep health among women.
papers.summary: This study analyzed data from 31,443 women in the Sister Study and found that maladaptive coping strategies mediated the relationship between perceived differential treatment based on race-ethnicity and poor sleep quality and insomnia symptoms, particularly among non-Hispanic Black and White women. The findings suggest that addressing maladaptive coping may reduce sleep disturbances.

papers.title: Digital surveillance or objective evidence? Wearable-derived data in insurance and legal medicine: A narrative review and medico-legal perspective.
papers.journal: Journal of forensic and legal medicine
papers.summary: This narrative review examines the evidentiary value and medico-legal limitations of wearable-derived data in insurance and legal medicine, concluding that such data cannot independently establish disability or credibility and require cautious, clinically contextualized interpretation.

papers.title: Nutritional Strategies for Recovery in Overhead Athletes: A Review.
papers.journal: HSS journal : the musculoskeletal journal of Hospital for Special Surgery
papers.summary: This review discusses nutritional strategies to optimize recovery in overhead athletes after intense exercise, focusing on replenishing glycogen, repairing muscle, rehydrating, and addressing inflammation and sleep. It provides guidance on carbohydrate and fluid intake, protein synthesis, and meal timing to support recovery and immune function.

papers.title: Understanding Alopecia Areata: An Integrative Review of Causes, Mechanisms, and Management Strategies.
papers.journal: Recent advances in inflammation & allergy drug discovery
papers.summary: This integrative review summarizes the pathophysiology of alopecia areata, including CD8+NKG2D+ T cell activation and loss of follicular immune privilege, and discusses conventional and emerging therapies such as JAK inhibitors, biologics, and regenerative approaches with promising initial findings.

papers.title: Complementary biomarkers or conflicting signals? DaT SPECT and synuclein skin biopsy in parkinsonian syndromes.
papers.summary: This retrospective study compared DaT SPECT imaging and phosphorylated alpha-synuclein skin biopsy in 86 patients with diagnostically uncertain parkinsonism. Combined testing increased sensitivity to 95.6% but reduced specificity to 59.9%, with 30.8% discordance, suggesting these biomarkers provide complementary information supporting the dual-origin model of alpha-synuclein propagation.

papers.title: Predictors of Paid Employment Status Among Individuals With Spinal Cord Injury in South Korea: An Exploratory Study Using Random Forest Analysis.
papers.summary: Using random forest analysis on survey data from 538 individuals with spinal cord injury in South Korea, this study identified predictors of paid employment, including higher household income, younger age, higher self-efficacy, better quality of life, access to vocational rehabilitation, and absence of disability benefits. These findings can inform policies to improve employment opportunities.

papers.title: Nasal breathing in pregnancy: a narrative review of physiology, dysregulation and therapeutic interventions.
papers.journal: The journal of maternal-fetal & neonatal medicine : the official journal of the European Association of Perinatal Medicine, the Federation of Asia and Oceania Perinatal Societies, the International Society of Perinatal Obstetricians
papers.summary: This narrative review discusses the physiological changes in nasal breathing during pregnancy, including hormonal effects on nasal mucosa, and explores potential consequences of nasal obstruction such as sleep-disordered breathing and adverse pregnancy outcomes. It also reviews interventions like pranayama and nasal dilators, noting that many require further study in pregnant populations.

papers.title: Annual review of selected scientific literature: A report of the Committee on Scientific Investigation of the American Academy of Restorative Dentistry.
papers.summary: This annual review by the American Academy of Restorative Dentistry summarizes selected 2025 dental literature across multiple disciplines including prosthodontics, implant dentistry, operative dentistry, and others. It aims to update restorative dentists on new materials, technologies, and evidence-based practices.

papers.title: Naloxone administration and toxicity signs and symptoms: An observational study using Canadian death investigation data
papers.summary: This observational study analyzed Canadian death investigation data from 2016-2017 to identify signs and substances associated with naloxone administration in acute drug toxicity deaths. Naloxone was administered to 45% of decedents, more often when opioids contributed to death, and was associated with classic opioid toxicity signs; when opioids did not contribute, opioid or stimulant detection was associated with administration.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
